rejected_changes.reason: I reject the proposed negative-to-uncertain change and retain my frozen negative. Here low-grade modifies chondral thinning itself, describing a low degree of thickness reduction in the named lateral compartment; it is not a bare low-grade OA/chondrosis diagnosis or an unspecified numbered grade. I treat that direct qualitative amount-of-loss statement as below-threshold evidence under the rubric, without inventing a particular percentage or named grading framework. No competing deeper lateral chondral defect is described. A measured extent is not needed to establish a below-depth-threshold negative; missing extent would matter for a positive if the depth criterion were established. The severe degeneration and complex tear refer to the lateral meniscus and must not supply cartilage severity. I understand the root concern that low-grade is not locally numerically calibrated, but requiring a numerical fraction for this direct low-degree thinning phrase would discard a qualitative below-threshold assessment that I judge informative. This is a disclosed report-level semantic inference, not an organizer-authorized crosswalk or proof from the images. My source-negative opinion predates proposal access, and I do not rely on the number or identities of agreeing readers. The root uncertainty and second reader original uncertainty are preserved as a real unresolved disagreement.
